messages:
incident-bot: Pager: high error rate on `decode-stream-*` pool — repeated CUDA OOMs on gpu-decode nodes. alert_id=INC-3623456789. paging oncall @ana :rotating_light:

ana: I'm on it. seeing OOM spikes across 3 nodes in us-west1-decode. metric: decode_oom_count up x40 in 2m.

mike: grabbing logs now, any customer hits?

anа: (typo) sorry, ana: yes — 5% request drop on streaming endpoints, some customers seeing partial responses. CS notified.

nora: tagging runtime team. can we throttle streaming tokens or enforce per-request max?

mike: quick mitigation options I can do now:
- enforce `max_tokens=1024` override at the route layer
- route heavy customers to cpu-fallback variant (higher latency)
- kick nodes to force kube to respin pods after mem leak

ana: do the max_tokens override + route big customers. I'll take node remediation.

raj: support: which customers affected? need to create incident update for accounts team.

priya: CS says two enterprise customers (acme-inc, brightshop) reported truncated streams and 502s. They're on Dedicated but using shared decode pool.

mike: applying temporary route override now. command:

```
# patch route to add header-based override
curl -X POST https://controlplane/api/routes/patch \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"selector":"streaming","override":{"max_tokens":1024}}'
```

mike: override pushed. verifying token limits...

ana: also set per-pod throttle to limit tokens in flight so KV cache doesn't explode. Applying a runtime flag on the decode service.

```
kubectl -n decode set env deploy/decode-runtime STREAM_MAX_INFLIGHT_TOKENS=200
kubectl -n decode rollout restart deploy/decode-runtime
```

mike: restarted — watch logs.

incident-bot: Update: error rate decreased 60% after overrides. decode_oom_count trending down.

nora: still seeing one node OOMing repeatedly: gpu-decode-07. looks like a leaked KV growth on certain long sessions.

ana: isolating node. cordon + drain then reprovision.

```
kubectl cordon gpu-decode-07
kubectl drain gpu-decode-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data
# node reprovision handled by autoscaler group
```

ana: drainage ok, pods moved. but might need a micro hotfix — limit max_output_tokens in the tokenizer layer for streaming path. mike, can you insert quick patch to generator config?

mike: yes, patching generator config map to set `max_output_tokens=900` for streaming path.

```
kubectl -n decode patch configmap gen-config -p '{"data":{"stream_max_output_tokens":"900"}}'
kubectl -n decode rollout restart deploy/decode-runtime
```

mike: patch applied. watching for OOMs.

incident-bot: New metrics: OOM events back to baseline, request drops reduced to ~0.8%.

priya: CS: reached out to acme-inc and brightshop with mitigation steps and ETA for follow-up. both want incident notes + impact timeframe.

eva: quick customer impact notes: timeframe 14:07-14:23 UTC, approx 16k requests affected, degraded streams and ~120 truncated responses.

nora: is this definitely max_tokens misconfig or memory leak triggered by unbounded generation?

ana: early hypothesis: mixed — we saw clients sending headers that bypassed route-level token caps (legacy SDK versions). combined with a KV cache corner case for very long prompts led to OOM. We'll need a fix in request validation + stronger header sanitization.

mike: adding a short-term ingress check to reject requests with client token override > 2000.

```
# ingress validation pseudo
if request.headers['X-Client-Max-Tokens'] > 2000:
  return 400
```

ana: i'll own a follow-up ticket to instrument KV cache growth and add per-session eviction. filing now.

incident-bot: oncall shift note — @ana handing to @nora in 30m for night coverage.

nora: I'll take handoff. summary for next oncall: overrides in place (route max_tokens=1024, gen-config max_output_tokens=900), node drained and reprovisioned, ingress validation patch scheduled, CS notified.

raj: support will send customer incident update with the impact numbers and mitigation steps. ETA 45m.

priya: filing follow-ups:
- SEV postmortem (owner: ana)
- KV cache instrumentation (owner: ana)
- Ingress header sanitization (owner: mike)
- SDK compatibility advisory to customers to not send X-Client-Max-Tokens (owner: priyа)

ana: assigning and tonights' oncall will triage the postmortem draft tomorrow morning. big thanks for quick responses. :thumbsup:

mike: leaving a note in deploy log: `hotfix/stream-token-limits` — we should rollback generator config change only after canary run 12h.

nora: I'll keep watch and escalate if OOMs return. marking thread for follow-up.

incident-bot: Incident INC-3623456789 updated: status=mitigated, severity=high -> monitoring.

ana: closing primary pager handoff. will collate logs and attach to postmortem.

mike: saved relevant logs to s3: s3://redwood-incident-logs/3623456789/ (contains `oom-trace.log`, `kube-events.json`).

priya: thanks team. I'll update customers once sevs doc ready.

nora: night shift ack.

(end of thread)
